review_notes: I read the whole file and the simp lemmas in PicZero/Basic.lean that it builds on. I grepped the tauceti sources for downstream uses of these declarations and found none outside this file, so the finding concerns the public interface rather than an observed client need. The other simp lemmas are consistent with their Basic.lean analogues: the `_obj` lemmas are non-simp in both files, and `mem_..._iff` unfolds one definitional layer, which looks intentional. I found no rewrite cycle or competing rules. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp behaviour.

findings.problem: The elementwise simp lemmas for the public natural transformations `rigidifiedPicardDegreeZeroToRelative` and `relativePicardDegreeZeroToRigidified` are all `@[simp] private`. Private lemmas cannot be named from other files. In particular, `relativePicardDegreeZeroFunctorι_app_toRelativeHom` is private, although its left side mentions only public objects and is the canonical computation of the public map. The same holds for `rigidifiedPicardDegreeZeroFunctorι_app_toRigidifiedHom`. The only public simp facts are the `_comp_` lemmas and `_FunctorIso_hom/inv`. These cover the composites of natural transformations but not the action on an element: `(rigidifiedPicardDegreeZeroToRelative f x₀ hx₀).app T a` followed by `(relativePicardDegreeZeroFunctorι f).app T`. Two things follow. A client that applies the iso to a section and then forgets to the full Picard presheaf cannot reduce it with simp. Users of the public `rigidifiedPicardDegreeZeroFunctorIso` also have to go through `_Hom` helpers that they cannot reference. The file's own proofs (`naturality`, `hom_inv_id`, `inv_hom_id`) rely on these private simp rules.
findings.proposed_change: Make the two inclusion-compatibility lemmas public, because they are the canonical normal forms. Their left sides need only public declarations once the `_Hom` helpers are inlined or exposed. Concretely, restate `relativePicardDegreeZeroFunctorι_app_toRelativeHom` as `(relativePicardDegreeZeroFunctorι f).app T ((rigidifiedPicardDegreeZeroToRelative f x₀ hx₀).app T a) = (rigidifiedPicardFunctorIso f x₀ hx₀).hom.app T ((rigidifiedPicardDegreeZeroFunctorι f x₀ hx₀).app T a)`. Do the same for the inverse direction. Give them non-private, descriptive names and keep `@[simp]`. Keep the `_Hom` helpers private, and keep `_app_apply` only as an internal unfolding aid. These statements are pointwise forms of the existing `_comp_` simp lemmas. Their left side is the more specific pattern and they do not loop, because they rewrite to the full-presheaf iso applied to the full-presheaf inclusion.
findings.benefit: Downstream files can simplify the composite of the degree-zero comparison with the inclusion on individual sections. At present the only way is to unfold the private helpers or use the categorical composition lemmas. The file's proofs then use only public simp lemmas, so the interface matches `relativePicardDegreeZeroFunctorι_app_mk` and `relativePicardDegreeZeroFunctorι_app_mkHom` in Basic.lean, which are public.
